name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,530

clue.text: Lead scientific study, maybe touched by extremely awful disease

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the following word, its very first and last letters

blocks.note: touched as in came into contact with, met
the first and last letters of awful
lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness

explanation.surface: A study of lead poisoning, perhaps, by a scientist affected by a dreadful illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy is jokey British slang for any catching illness, as in 'don't give me the lurgy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallurgy is the science of metals, and lead is one such metal, so studying lead is an example of the discipline.

clue.text: Look bad-tempered in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means we go by how a word is spoken rather than how it is written

blocks.note: mean can describe someone nasty or bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Someone giving a cross glance while chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mien is a person's appearance or bearing, especially the expression showing their mood, so a look.

clue.text: Characteristic habit to cheat

blocks.note: first meaning: a mannerism or peculiar habit
second meaning: a verb, to deceive or swindle someone

explanation.surface: Someone whose typical behaviour is cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a personal quirk or mannerism, and the verb means to deceive or hoodwink someone.

clue.text: Attack unlimited gambling on tense final of judo

indicators.note: without limits means the word loses its boundaries, the letters at each end
on means the next pieces are placed alongside, following on from the first
final of asks for only the closing letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: playing, as at the tables, is gambling
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
the final letter of judo

explanation.surface: A judo contest's last bout as the subject of reckless betting.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is an idiom meaning to assault them physically or verbally.

clue.text: Relative ambition that's heartless and immoral

indicators.note: without a heart, the inner letters are dropped and only the outside pair is kept

blocks.note: an uncle is a family relative
the outer letters of ambition

explanation.surface: A family member whose ruthless drive makes them wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean can mean morally impure or sinful, so it serves as a synonym for wicked conduct.

clue.text: South African ready to visit on vacation glum adult family member

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters of the word stay
a visitor goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: glum with its middle emptied
ready is slang for cash, and the rand is South Africa's currency
A is the old film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A South African, poised to go on holiday, looks gloomy about a visit to a grown-up relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' is British slang for money, so South African ready is the rand.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandma is a grandmother, the parent of one's parent and so a relation in the family.

clue.text: Man, for example, that's deceived, receiving no protection

indicators.note: with no protection the word loses its outer covering, the letters at each end

blocks.note: to mislead someone is to deceive them

explanation.surface: A man who has been fooled is left unprotected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so it is an example of the general word for an island.

clue.text: Cocktail that creates a cool ambience around 6?

definitions.text: that creates a cool ambience around 6?

blocks.note: first meaning: a drink of vodka with cranberry and grapefruit juice

blocks.clueFragment: that creates a cool ambience around 6?
blocks.note: second meaning: the cooling air off the water that surrounds an island, the answer to 6

explanation.surface: A drink that sets a relaxed mood on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half refers to 6 across, an island, and the air blowing in from the water around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocktail is named for the wind blowing off the ocean, which is what freshens the air of an island.

clue.text: Reached tax arrangement with authority

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A deal on taxes agreed with a public body.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex cathedra is Latin for 'from the chair', describing pronouncements made with the full authority of office, especially papal.

clue.text: Priests outside mark old feast day

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the second

blocks.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Clergy gathering outdoors to celebrate a traditional holy day.
explanation.walkthrough: Lammas, 1 August, was the English harvest festival when loaves of the new wheat were blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas is the traditional English harvest celebration on the first of August, a holy day now mostly lapsed.

clue.text: Improve the minds of some disenchanted, if youthful characters

indicators.note: some means only part of the following run of characters is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third; characters says we are dealing with letters

explanation.surface: Educating young people who have lost their illusions.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone so as to improve them morally or intellectually.

clue.text: Risk briefly carrying horse in old vehicle

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
carrying means holding something inside

blocks.note: to chance it is to take a risk
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: Taking a gamble by transporting a horse in an antique vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an early open motor coach used for day outings, now obsolete.

clue.text: He's a kind eccentric, one with little up top though

definitions.text: one with little up top though

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentle oddball who is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little up top' suggests a lack of brains, but here it means a lack of hair; 'though' contrasts with the kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead has a closely shaved head, so very little hair on top.

clue.text: Worth Rome writer ignoring argumentative individual at intervals?

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving letters out of the phrase before it
at intervals tells us the dropped letters are spread out, not in one block

blocks.note: taken as written
a row is an argument, so someone who rows is argumentative

explanation.surface: Whether a Roman author has value if he dismisses a quarrelsome critic now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: R, O, W, E and R are struck from the phrase one by one, in order but not together, leaving M, E, R, I, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is the quality of deserving praise, so it means value or excellence.

clue.text: Male boss undermined by flier displaying baffling jargon

indicators.note: in a down clue, being undermined puts the next piece underneath, so it follows

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
an umbo is the raised boss in the centre of a shield
a jumbo is a jumbo jet, a large aircraft

explanation.surface: A male manager's authority sapped by a pilot spouting nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is the knob on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo-jumbo is meaningless or obscure language intended to confuse, so incomprehensible talk.

clue.text: University and school rent regularly overlooked, not cut

indicators.note: overlooking letters at regular steps means every other letter is skipped

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters of this phrase

explanation.surface: A campus and school whose rent payments are regularly forgotten, though not reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn means sheared, so unshorn describes hair or wool left untrimmed.

clue.text: Short bouncy type, Liverpool player perhaps, acted as captain

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its final letter

blocks.note: a skipper is one who skips, hopping along
Liverpool FC play in red and are nicknamed the Reds

explanation.surface: A small, energetic Liverpool footballer who led the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool is an English football club whose players are known as the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: To skipper is to captain a side or a boat, so the past tense means led as captain.

clue.text: Rule out treasure being scattered in grave

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter named before it is taken away
scattered things are strewn about in no order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: R is an abbreviation for rule
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ruling out that treasure was strewn about in a burial site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place, but it is the adjective meaning solemn.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and severe in manner, just as grave describes a serious, solemn demeanour.

clue.text: Prepared to be given a diet of cheese?

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
someone given a diet is fed

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to eat nothing but cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split: the answer read as two words is literally cheese-fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being briefed means having been given instructions in advance, so made ready for a task.

clue.text: Stack of food that describes dinner essentially

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence or core, so the centre letters are taken
to describe a shape is to draw a line round it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: food is fuel for the body
the middle two letters of dinner

explanation.surface: A pile of food served up at an evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stack' suggests a heap of food, but it is a ship's chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A stack is a chimney, and a ship's funnel is the chimney through which its engine smoke escapes.

clue.text: Reveal resort in which to stick around endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word has its last letter cut off
turned around, the letters are read in the opposite direction
in which places the next piece inside the resort word

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar or haunt, a place one resorts to
to glue is to stick

explanation.surface: Disclosing a holiday spot where one can hang about forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' suggests a holiday town, but it is a place frequented, here a disreputable one.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge is to make known information that was private or secret, so to disclose it.

clue.text: Current unfinished row between Left and Right in Curacao, say

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is missing
between means placed inside, flanked on either side

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a queue is a row of people waiting
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A political dispute between left and right on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Curacao is a Caribbean island, but it also names an orange-flavoured spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Curacao is an orange-flavoured sweet spirit, one example of the general class of after-dinner liqueurs.

clue.text: Brilliant amateur, first from blocks during fast time

indicators.note: first from asks for only the opening letter of the next word
during means within a stretch of time, so these pieces go inside

blocks.note: AM is an abbreviation for amateur
the first letter of blocks
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A talented amateur sprinter getting off the blocks quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast time' suggests a quick race result, but fast here means going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes something softly glowing or flickering, or wit that is light and sparkling.

clue.text: Question over American pet food, missing kilo generates complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above, so ahead of the rest
missing means a letter is absent from the word before it

blocks.note: QU is an abbreviation for question
kibble is the American name for dry pellet food for pets
K is the abbreviation for kilo

explanation.surface: A query about US pet food sold short in weight leads to a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A quibble is a minor objection or petty criticism, so a small grievance.

clue.text: Consent from Germany to criticise its wartime ally

blocks.note: ja is German for yes
to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Germany agreeing to condemn the nation it fought alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Second World War Japan was one of the Axis powers alongside Germany, so Germany's ally.

clue.text: Night owls partial to claret but not steaks reportedly?

definitions.text: Night owls partial to claret but not steaks reportedly?

blocks.clueFragment: Night owls partial to claret but not steaks reportedly?
blocks.note: surface reading: people who stay up late, enjoy red wine and avoid steak

blocks.clueFragment: Night owls partial to claret but not steaks reportedly?
blocks.note: setter's reading: nocturnal creatures who drink blood (claret is slang for it) and fear wooden stakes, which sound like steaks

explanation.surface: Late-night revellers who love red wine but do not eat steak.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is old slang for blood, and 'steaks reportedly' points to the sound of stakes, the wooden weapons that kill these creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The undead of folklore are active at night, drink human blood and are destroyed by a stake through the heart.

clue.text: Course of electrotherapy probably surpasses other medication initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: of electrotherapy probably surpasses other medication
blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words after 'of'

explanation.surface: A course of electric treatment that probably beats any drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a course of treatment, but it is a racecourse; Epsom is the Surrey racecourse that hosts the Derby, and Epsom salts are a medicine too.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous English racecourse, home to the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Inadequate tool for drawing

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word is not given in full

blocks.note: a plane is a woodworking tool for smoothing

explanation.surface: A tool that is no good for sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scale drawing, such as an architect's diagram of a building from above.

clue.text: Difficult to look restrained after damage in French city

indicators.note: restrained means held in, so one piece is held inside another
after places the next piece behind the earlier one

blocks.note: to mar something is to damage it
to see is to look
ill can mean difficult, as in ill-tempered or ill at ease

explanation.surface: Struggling to keep a calm face after harm done in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille is the major Mediterranean port city in the south of France.

clue.text: Culinary plant from Mali's absolutely revolutionary

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow
a revolution turns things over, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A herb from the African country Mali that is radically new.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb used widely in cooking, especially in Italian dishes.

clue.text: Scraps inequality

blocks.note: first meaning: bits and pieces
second meaning: a disparity or imbalance

explanation.surface: Fights about unfairness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' reads like fights, but it means leftover fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are miscellaneous leftovers, and the word also means a difference in advantage between two sides.

clue.text: Fish possibly once served raw, eaten with moreish sides

indicators.note: served up as a dish, the ingredients are prepared and rearranged
the sides of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the two edge letters of moreish

explanation.surface: Fish perhaps served as sashimi, eaten with tasty side dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like food, but Michael Fish was a long-serving BBC television forecaster, now retired, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Fish presented British television forecasts for decades, so he is an example of a former forecaster.
